findings.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139 — P1 (99% confidence), verbatim `const index = backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""));` followed by `await prisma.user.update(...)`: concurrent credential authorizations can both read the same unused backup-code array and validate the same index before either unconditional write records `null`, so one supposedly single-use code grants more than one successful login.

apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:12 — Severity P2, confidence 99%, verbatim `// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup`: the newly added backup-code login and backup-code 2FA-disable recovery flows have no automated acceptance coverage, so either core recovery path can regress completely while this changed suite still passes.

apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx:5 — P1, confidence 95: `import { Label, TextField } from "@calcom/ui";` imports `TextField`, but the checked-in `@calcom/ui` implementation exports no `TextField`, so TypeScript cannot compile this new component until it imports an available field component or adds that export.

packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139 — P1 (confidence 92%): Two concurrent login requests using the same backup code can both authenticate because each reads the unconsumed array (`"const index = backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll(\"-\", \"\"));"`) before either unconditional update, then both write the same consumed version and return success.

apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:278 — P2 (confidence 99%): Clicking Copy in a browser without Clipboard API support or with denied clipboard permission either throws or rejects unhandled while the UI immediately claims success (`"navigator.clipboard.writeText(backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode).join(\"\\n\"));"` followed by `"showToast(t(\"backup_codes_copied\"), \"success\");"`), leaving the user without the only copied recovery codes.

packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:49 — P2 (85% confidence): the unrelated global password-field change `tabIndex={-1}` removes the visibility toggle from keyboard tab order across every PasswordField, expanding a “2fa backup codes” task into unrequested shared-component behavior.

packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:121 — P1 confidence 99% verbatim `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` makes password verification depend only on attacker-controlled nonempty `totpCode`, so a caller submitting any dummy TOTP plus a stolen valid `backupCode` reaches the new backup-code branch at line 131 and obtains a session without knowing the account password.

packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:149 — P2 confidence 97% verbatim `await prisma.user.update({` overwrites `backupCodes` without atomically asserting/removing the matched code, so concurrent requests that both read the same still-valid backup code can each authenticate before either write, violating its one-time-use security guarantee.

apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:116 — Advisory [P2, confidence 95%]: `expect(download.suggestedFilename()).toBe("cal-backup-codes.txt")` only verifies the download name, so an empty or malformed backup-code file still passes while users receive unusable recovery credentials; assert the saved download contains the generated, correctly formatted codes (rebuttal: filename checking is still a useful smoke assertion).

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:12 — Severity P2, confidence 99%, verbatim `// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup`: the newly added backup-code login and backup-code 2FA-disable recovery flows have no automated acceptance coverage, so either core recovery path can regress completely while this changed suite still passes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds significant new backup code functionality for both login (in next-auth-options.ts) and disabling 2FA (in disable.ts), but the test file explicitly has a TODO comment acknowledging missing test coverage for these flows. The finding correctly identifies that the new backup code login and backup code 2FA-disable recovery paths lack automated test coverage. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a bug but an important review concern grounded in specific code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx:5 — P1, confidence 95: `import { Label, TextField } from "@calcom/ui";` imports `TextField`, but the checked-in `@calcom/ui` implementation exports no `TextField`, so TypeScript cannot compile this new component until it imports an available field component or adds that export.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that @calcom/ui does not export TextField, but looking at the diff, we can see that TextField is already being used successfully in other files in this codebase. For example, in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx line 8, TextField was previously imported from @calcom/ui (before being changed to PasswordField). The diff also shows TextField being used in the existing TwoFactor.tsx component. The finding makes an unverifiable claim about what @calcom/ui exports that contradicts evidence in the diff itself showing TextField is a valid export.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139 — P1 (confidence 92%): Two concurrent login requests using the same backup code can both authenticate because each reads the unconsumed array (`"const index = backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll(\"-\", \"\"));"`) before either unconditional update, then both write the same consumed version and return success.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that backup code validation in next-auth-options.ts reads the backup codes array, checks if the code exists with indexOf(), then updates the database to mark it as used. There's no transaction or locking mechanism. Two concurrent requests with the same backup code could both read the array before either writes, both find the code valid at the same index, and both successfully authenticate. This is a classic TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use) race condition that could allow a backup code to be used multiple times.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:278 — P2 (confidence 99%): Clicking Copy in a browser without Clipboard API support or with denied clipboard permission either throws or rejects unhandled while the UI immediately claims success (`"navigator.clipboard.writeText(backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode).join(\"\\n\"));"` followed by `"showToast(t(\"backup_codes_copied\"), \"success\");"`), leaving the user without the only copied recovery codes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 278-282 that navigator.clipboard.writeText() is called and immediately followed by showToast() with success message, without any .then()/.catch() or try/catch handling. The clipboard API returns a Promise that can reject if permissions are denied or the API is unavailable. The code assumes success without awaiting or handling the promise rejection, which means the success toast will show even if the copy operation fails. This is a real bug where users could be misled into thinking their backup codes were copied when they weren't.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:49 — P2 (85% confidence): the unrelated global password-field change `tabIndex={-1}` removes the visibility toggle from keyboard tab order across every PasswordField, expanding a “2fa backup codes” task into unrequested shared-component behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show adding tabIndex={-1} to the PasswordField's visibility toggle button at line 50. This is a real change that affects all PasswordField usages across the codebase, not just the 2FA backup codes feature. The finding correctly identifies this as scope creep - modifying a shared component's keyboard accessibility behavior as part of an unrelated feature. While this may be intentional (to prevent tab focus on the toggle), it's a valid concern that this change affects all password fields globally and wasn't explicitly part of the backup codes feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:121 — P1 confidence 99% verbatim `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` makes password verification depend only on attacker-controlled nonempty `totpCode`, so a caller submitting any dummy TOTP plus a stolen valid `backupCode` reaches the new backup-code branch at line 131 and obtains a session without knowing the account password.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that password verification depends on `totpCode` being nonempty, but looking at the actual diff, the password verification happens BEFORE the 2FA checks. At lines 119-126 in the original code (not shown but implied by context), password is verified with `verifyPassword(credentials.password, user.password)`. The backup code branch at line 131 only runs AFTER password verification has already passed. The condition `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` at line 131 is for choosing between backup code vs TOTP verification, not for bypassing password verification. The finding misreads the code flow - password verification is independent of the 2FA method chosen.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:149 — P2 confidence 97% verbatim `await prisma.user.update({` overwrites `backupCodes` without atomically asserting/removing the matched code, so concurrent requests that both read the same still-valid backup code can each authenticate before either write, violating its one-time-use security guarantee.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in next-auth-options.ts, the backup code validation reads backupCodes, checks if the user-supplied code exists in the array (indexOf), then separately updates the database to null out that code. Between the read and write, there's no atomic operation or locking. Two concurrent login requests with the same valid backup code could both pass the indexOf check before either write completes, allowing the same backup code to be used twice. This is a real race condition security vulnerability in the one-time-use backup code implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:116 — Advisory [P2, confidence 95%]: `expect(download.suggestedFilename()).toBe("cal-backup-codes.txt")` only verifies the download name, so an empty or malformed backup-code file still passes while users receive unusable recovery credentials; assert the saved download contains the generated, correctly formatted codes (rebuttal: filename checking is still a useful smoke assertion).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test at line 116 only checks the filename of the downloaded backup codes file, not its content. The diff shows a TODO comment at line 119 acknowledging 'TODO: check file content', confirming this is an incomplete test. Since backup codes are critical for account recovery (the entire feature being added), verifying the file contains valid, correctly formatted codes is a legitimate test coverage concern. This is not a bug (the feature works), but it's a specific, diff-grounded observation about incomplete test coverage for security-critical functionality.
